speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To begin my assessment, can you tell me how many weeks gestation you were at birth, and what was your initial Apgar score?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the information provided, the baby was born at 33 weeks gestation with respiratory distress starting 2 hours after birth. Given the prematurity, is there any evidence of maternal diabetes or infection, and have any initial tests like blood gas analysis or chest X-ray been performed?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTNB).

The clinical picture of respiratory distress with grunting, retractions, and cyanosis in a late preterm infant (33 weeks) born with an uneventful pregnancy and no mention of meconium aspiration or maternal infection is highly suggestive of TTNB. The lack of severe infection signs and the specific timing (2 hours post-birth) support this over sepsis or early-onset pneumonia.
